rv.q: In the lead role, newcomer Mandipa Kabanda tears through the dialogue at a pace not seen since Ivo van Hove’s More Stately Mansions, matching the other actors in urgency and drive.

This tension is underlined during the tumultuous trial scene, where the Inquisitor meticulously presents his arguments against heresy. It’s simple but compelling, with all six actors sitting solemnly in a row, the men draped in black oversized hoodies, while Joan wears masculine dress, in defiance of gendered expectations.
On the contrary, Laing’s defamiliarizing of the historical context renders the scene all the more compelling.
Saint Joan , whilst valiant in its efforts to immerse the story into the 21st century, struggles to find a clear method.
Saint Joan is a striking and necessary piece of theatre – urgent, human and impossible to look away from.

cn.t: Stewart Laing's modernized Saint Joan divides critics with its stripped-back, inventive approach. Most praise the bold directorial vision, though some find the contemporary reimagining misses the mark.
